scope: Original streaming/revision/speaker-aware reasoning proposal; seven system architectures, five resources in each other category
selection: Purposive relevance selection, unranked; not an exhaustive or independently reproduced survey

categories.title: Reasoning and system designs
categories.label: tab:systems
categories.selection: Seven anchors span explicit and latent listening-time reasoning, timed text-backbone speech, concurrent formulation/articulation, two asynchronous interaction/thinking designs, and native parallel text/function heads. Moshi is compared separately in the synchronization shortlist. The other three categories retain five entries each.

rows.name: Think while listening
cells: Moshi/Helium 7B temporal + depth transformers; parallel user/agent audio and text. Silent text reasoning is interleaved with ASR and answer text; completeness and preference supervision.
Study-specific code/weights not located; released Moshi is a different checkpoint.
Recipe only; full 1.8M-example spoken-CoT collection not located.

rows.name: FLAIR
cells: Qwen2.5-7B + streaming Parakeet encoder + autoregressive speech decoder. Listening steps feed a soft vocabulary-weighted latent embedding; full-context teacher trains a causal inference model.
Dedicated implementation/checkpoint not located.
ELBO/SFT recipe; full mixture not located.

rows.name: MiniCPM-o 4.5
cells: Qwen3-8B (~9B system). Omni-Flow serializes timed windows. Main LLM predicts text/listen decisions; a small Llama/S3 speech-token decoder and streaming flow decoder synthesize audio.
Inference + realtime demo and weights; Apache-2.0.
General fine-tuning tools; complete duplex recipe and mixture not established.

rows.name: StepAudio 3 Realtime
cells: Step 3.7 Flash MoE (196B total/11B active) + AuT speech encoder. Two concurrent audio-LLM processes share parameters: private formulation and articulation, with playback-aware pacing and async tools.
Report/project demos; Realtime code/weights not located. Earlier Step releases are not this model.
Recipe; full training code/mixture not located.

rows.name: Realtime-Venus
cells: MiniCPM-o 4.5-derived 9B Audio/Omni frontend; causal 1 s chunks, persistent context, and an asynchronous backend. A harness returns backend text to the speaking frontend.
Inference/harness + Audio/Omni weights; Apache-2.0. Demo integration is Omni-based.
Methods; complete training package/mixture not located.

rows.name: DuplexOmni
cells: Qwen3-Omni Thinker/Talker interaction model; 480 ms slices and persistent speech context. A separate pluggable thinking layer returns streaming feedback and can be stopped. Reported full configuration uses Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite.
Inference, training and data-pipeline code; weights released. Source Apache-2.0; upstream terms apply.
Writer-Director metadata + one generated shard; not the full ~9 TB corpus.

rows.name: NemotronLabs VoiceChat
cells: 11B system: Nemotron Nano 9B v2 + 80 ms FastConformer features; parallel text/function heads, auxiliary RNN-T and separately trained streaming TTS. No user ASR transcript fed into the LLM. Tool execution currently disables barge-in.
NeMo runtime branch + weights; OpenMDW-1.1 weights. Not a Moshi decoder.
Training methods and sources; full pipeline and mixture not established.

categories.title: Synchronization and temporal interfaces
categories.label: tab:synchronization
categories.selection: Five directly relevant works cover clock-aligned serialization, codec-rate multi-stream generation, speech/listening/action alignment, adaptive scheduling, and representation-level speaker/listener coupling. The last is an analysis, not another model architecture.

rows.name: SyncLLM
cells: Llama 3-8B with deduplicated HuBERT units (25 Hz before deduplication); periodic speaker/chunk tokens align the sequence to a real-world clock. Speculative user chunks are replaced by observed input.
Synchronous full-duplex scheduling despite variable token counts; evaluates processing/network delay.
Official paper/demos; model code/weights not located. Clock alignment alone does not establish revision correctness.

rows.name: Moshi
cells: Mimi 12.5 Hz (80 ms) frames; temporal transformer plus depth transformer model parallel audio streams and aligned inner-monologue text.
A concrete shared acoustic grid, streaming speech generation, and low-latency duplex interaction.
Inference and fine-tuning code + weights. MIT/Apache code; model CC BY 4.0. A frame clock is not a semantic commitment policy.

rows.name: DuplexSLA
cells: Step-Audio 2 mini-derived ~7B model. A 160 ms clock joins two 80 ms listening features, one text/four audio tokens, and up to ten action tokens; queued action spillover and dual-side ASR.
Native concurrent speaking/listening plus timestamp-aligned planning, control and tool events.
Official repository says inference, weights and benchmark are forthcoming. Not a released checkpoint as of cutoff.

rows.name: AdaptDuplex
cells: Qwen3-Omni Thinker/Talker; 0.48/0.64/0.96 s windows, bounded text lead, and up to four indexed backend jobs. Cancelled/stale results are suppressed before injection.
Adaptive granularity and explicit backend-result admission already exist; not a new idea to simply cancel a stale job.
Paper verified; dedicated code/checkpoint not located. Joint speaker-owned state and actual playback still need controlled tests.

rows.name: Synchronization and Turn-Taking
cells: Moshi--Moshi appointment dialogues: lagged CKA compares speaker/listener hidden states; causal probes classify end-of-interpausal-unit hold/non-hold events.
Representational coupling and predictive timing signals vary with noise and speech activity bias.
Preprint; study artifacts not located. Restricted task; CKA/probe success is not causal reasoning consistency.

categories.title: Benchmarks for the proposal
categories.label: tab:benchmarks
categories.selection: Five complementary tests cover streaming reasoning onset, grounded task completion, natural disfluency/tool use, post-interruption state revision, and speaker/addressee control. Their scores should not be merged into a leaderboard.

rows.name: SRQA
cells: TTS/LLM-rewritten ARC-E/C, SIQA, PIQA, GSM8K; mostly single-turn synthetic spoken questions.
Reasoning accuracy and post-question chain-of-thought delay; prefix sufficiency controls.
Construction in ICLR paper; released audio/eval package not located. CoT onset is not first useful audible answer.

rows.name: tau-Voice
cells: 278 airline/retail/telecom tasks; clean/realistic speech; full-duplex simulated user. ICML 2026 (PMLR 306).
Grounded pass@1, interruption behavior and voice interaction quality; tool/task consequences.
Code/tasks/simulator; provider APIs needed. Virtual time decouples simulation from wall-clock runtime; pin original revision (repo now tau3-bench).

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v3
cells: Human recordings, five disfluency types, chained tools across four task domains.
Tool-selection F1, argument accuracy, pass@1; first response, tool and completion latencies.
Scoring/inference code + recording download. Tool F1 is not task success; exact and judge-assisted argument scores differ.

rows.name: EchoChain
cells: 200 controlled interrupted conversations; synthesized user/barge-in audio; four closed realtime models; paired half-duplex control.
Conversation/criterion pass rates and failures: contextual inertia, interruption amnesia, objective displacement.
Paper, prompts and examples verified; standalone code/audio release not located. Does not cover backchannels, side speech or detailed acoustic timing.

rows.name: Duplex-MPE
cells: 2,000 matched pairs / 4,000 synthetic streams; 3--4 human roles plus assistant; explicit/implicit address.
Response initiation, answer accuracy, silence preservation, floor release; speaker-owned update controls.
Paper verified; standalone code/audio release not located. Floor release is conditional on the assistant already speaking.

categories.title: Training data and supervision sources
categories.label: tab:data
categories.selection: Five natural conversational resources are chosen for channel separation, temporal/speaker annotations, or task events. These are resources to construct supervision, not five existing reasoning-training mixtures.

rows.name: SmoothConv
cells: 100.53 h; Chinese; natural multi-party, multi-channel audio.
Expert transcripts, speaker IDs, turn state, timing and paralinguistic labels.
HF release; CC BY-NC 4.0. Control/speaker supervision; shares source conversations with DuplexConv.

rows.name: DuplexConv
cells: 2,000.21 h; Chinese; natural multi-party, multi-channel audio.
LLM-assisted transcripts, per-track VAD, speaker/turn segments, acoustic and scene labels.
HF release; CC BY-NC 4.0. Larger timing pretraining; audit labels and split by underlying source session.

rows.name: otoSpeech Task
cells: 20.006 h; 58 English sessions; two-speaker 48 kHz channels; seven task types.
Synchronized events, stimuli, participant artifacts and task-related metadata.
Gated HF files/contact acceptance; CC BY 4.0. Task-evidence alignment; verify outcomes before treating as reasoning labels.

rows.name: otoSpeech conversational
cells: 280 h raw / 141 h curated; English; separate speaker channels; curated 44.1 kHz.
Session/speaker metadata, redactions, surveys; natural overlap and timing.
Gated HF files/contact acceptance; CC BY 4.0. Listening robustness; curated hours are a subset, not extra data.

rows.name: Open Yap 1K
cells: 1,000 h; 1,602 English conversations; 239 speakers; separate 48 kHz channels.
Word-level transcripts, speaker/device metadata, overlap and turn-gap statistics.
Public sample; full corpus by request/Data Use Agreement. Natural conversation, not an ungated full release.

papers.title: Can Speech LLMs Think while Listening?
papers.problem: Direct prior work for both semantic sufficiency and revision-aware reasoning in the original proposal.
papers.method: Moshi / Helium 7B + Mimi Text monologue interleaves streaming ASR, silent text CoT and answer text alongside audio. Moshi temporal + depth transformers; reasoning tokens have no corresponding spoken output. Question-completeness supervision starts CoT early; correctness and length DPO improve adaptation.
papers.results: Authors report 2.4× mean reasoning accuracy over Moshi and about 70% lower reasoning latency without accuracy loss.
papers.relevance: Direct prior work for both semantic sufficiency and revision-aware reasoning in the original proposal.
papers.limitations: Single-turn spoken reasoning suite; 480 ms ASR look-ahead; benchmark/model release not located. Reasoning latency is not first useful spoken answer latency.

comparison: Moshi/Helium 7B temporal + depth transformers; parallel user/agent audio and text. Silent text reasoning is interleaved with ASR and answer text; completeness and preference supervision.
Study-specific code/weights not located; released Moshi is a different checkpoint.
Recipe only; full 1.8M-example spoken-CoT collection not located.
TTS/LLM-rewritten ARC-E/C, SIQA, PIQA, GSM8K; mostly single-turn synthetic spoken questions.
Reasoning accuracy and post-question chain-of-thought delay; prefix sufficiency controls.
Construction in ICLR paper; released audio/eval package not located. CoT onset is not first useful audible answer.

papers.title: The Silent Thought: Modeling Internal Cognition in Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models via Latent Reasoning
papers.problem: Listening-time silence/padding does not exploit ongoing latent reasoning.
papers.method: Soft vocabulary-weighted latent embeddings; ELBO/SFT from a full-context expert into a causal inference model.
papers.results: Authors evaluate reasoning and interaction improvements over their pretraining-only baseline; no independent reproduction or unified leaderboard in this review.
papers.relevance: Direct alternative to explicit prefix chain-of-thought and a close prior to think-while-listening claims.
papers.limitations: Complete mixture and dedicated artifacts not located; teacher access to future context is training supervision, not permitted evaluation evidence.

comparison: Qwen2.5-7B + streaming Parakeet encoder + autoregressive speech decoder. Listening steps feed a soft vocabulary-weighted latent embedding; full-context teacher trains a causal inference model.
Dedicated implementation/checkpoint not located.
ELBO/SFT recipe; full mixture not located.

papers.title: MiniCPM-o 4.5: Towards Real-Time Full-Duplex Omni-Modal Interaction
papers.problem: Concrete open alternative to Moshi for a streaming encoder + text reasoning backbone.
papers.method: Qwen3-8B; about 9B total Omni-Flow serializes time windows of audio, video and assistant output; [listen] when silent. Small Llama speech-token decoder + S3 tokens + streaming flow-matching waveform decoder. Explicit listen/speak decision; main LLM generates text, separate decoder generates speech.
papers.results: In the paper’s ablation, 1.0 s windows outperform 0.1 / 0.2 s on the tested language tasks.
papers.relevance: Concrete open alternative to Moshi for a streaming encoder + text reasoning backbone.
papers.limitations: Shorter windows trade response opportunity against language competence. A full duplex-training mixture is not released.

comparison: Qwen3-8B (~9B system). Omni-Flow serializes timed windows. Main LLM predicts text/listen decisions; a small Llama/S3 speech-token decoder and streaming flow decoder synthesize audio.
Inference + realtime demo and weights; Apache-2.0.
General fine-tuning tools; complete duplex recipe and mixture not established.

papers.title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
papers.problem: Strong reference for coordinating speech, private reasoning and tool execution.
papers.method: Step 3.7 Flash MoE: 196B total / 11B active AuT encoder + adapter; user and model audio feed shared conversational context. Streaming speech generator; detailed generator internals are less specified than the LLM. Listen / speak / start / end states; private think-while-speaking; asynchronous tools.
papers.results: Authors report 98.9 Overall on Artificial Analysis Full-Duplex Bench and 56.0% macro task success on τ-Voice.
papers.relevance: Strong reference for coordinating speech, private reasoning and tool execution.
papers.limitations: Reported benchmark scores use their own protocol. No StepAudio 3 Realtime checkpoint or training release was located; earlier Step-Audio releases are separate models.

comparison: Step 3.7 Flash MoE (196B total/11B active) + AuT speech encoder. Two concurrent audio-LLM processes share parameters: private formulation and articulation, with playback-aware pacing and async tools.
Report/project demos; Realtime code/weights not located. Earlier Step releases are not this model.
Recipe; full training code/mixture not located.

papers.title: Realtime-Venus: A full-duplex interaction system with asynchronous delegation
papers.problem: Released architecture and harness for testing revisions while a backend task is pending.
papers.method: MiniCPM-o 4.5-derived Audio and Omni frontends; 9B family One-second causal chunks; retained frontend state; separate background task loop. Frontend text and speech generation; text results admitted back into the stream. Explicit foreground / delegation outputs; harness executes background jobs asynchronously.
papers.results: Audio variant reports continuation of 97% / 88% / 86% for backchannel / other-directed / background speech in FDB v1.5.
papers.relevance: Released architecture and harness for testing revisions while a backend task is pending.
papers.limitations: Audio and Omni evaluations differ. Released harness/demo integration is Omni-based; do not assume every paper setting is reproduced.

comparison: MiniCPM-o 4.5-derived 9B Audio/Omni frontend; causal 1 s chunks, persistent context, and an asynchronous backend. A harness returns backend text to the speaking frontend.
Inference/harness + Audio/Omni weights; Apache-2.0. Demo integration is Omni-based.
Methods; complete training package/mixture not located.

papers.title: DuplexOmni: Real-Time Listening, Seeing, Thinking, and Speaking for Full-Duplex Interaction
papers.problem: Real-time dialogue must continue while slower multimodal reasoning and tools run asynchronously.
papers.method: Qwen3-Omni-derived interaction Thinker/Talker on 480 ms slices, separate pluggable thinking layer, streaming feedback/reset and Writer-Director supervision.
papers.results: Table 1 reports interaction, streaming understanding, WER and latency for the full system with Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite. Shared audited numeric profiles retain missing values and convert WER fractions to percent; no independent reproduction.
papers.relevance: Released layered baseline for think/listen/speak concurrency, explicit reasoning interruption and synthesized causal timing labels.
papers.limitations: Reported full configuration is not an all-open backend comparison. English/video weaknesses are acknowledged. Metadata and one shard do not constitute the full approximately 9 TB generated corpus; the ToR aggregate and latency endpoint are not harmonized across studies.

comparison: Qwen3-Omni Thinker/Talker interaction model; 480 ms slices and persistent speech context. A separate pluggable thinking layer returns streaming feedback and can be stopped. Reported full configuration uses Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite.
Inference, training and data-pipeline code; weights released. Source Apache-2.0; upstream terms apply.
Writer-Director metadata + one generated shard; not the full ~9 TB corpus.

papers.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
papers.problem: Native tool calling must coexist with low-latency speech, user transcription and conversational turn control.
papers.method: Nemotron Nano 9B v2 with streaming FastConformer, parallel text/function heads, auxiliary shared-encoder RNN-T and independently trained persistent TTS on an 80 ms feature grid.
papers.results: Table 4 reports FDB-v3 tool F1, argument accuracy and pass@1; the shared profile includes its imported Gemini references and a separately attributed GPT-Realtime benchmark context reference. No independent reproduction.
papers.relevance: An open text-backbone alternative to Moshi and serialized action tokens; exposes separate speech, transcription and native function channels.
papers.limitations: User ASR transcript is not the LLM input. Tool execution substitutes silence during training, predefined acknowledgments at runtime, and currently prevents barge-in. Approximately two-minute context, limited tool composition and background-speech robustness; complete assembled training mixture not established.

comparison: 11B system: Nemotron Nano 9B v2 + 80 ms FastConformer features; parallel text/function heads, auxiliary RNN-T and separately trained streaming TTS. No user ASR transcript fed into the LLM. Tool execution currently disables barge-in.
NeMo runtime branch + weights; OpenMDW-1.1 weights. Not a Moshi decoder.
Training methods and sources; full pipeline and mixture not established.

papers.title: Beyond Turn-Based Interfaces: Synchronous LLMs as Full-Duplex Dialogue Agents
papers.problem: Variable text/unit sequence length must still track a real acoustic clock.
papers.method: Periodic speaker/chunk boundaries plus deduplicated semantic units and speculative user prediction/replacement.
papers.results: Authors demonstrate synchronous full-duplex generation and evaluate processing/network delay; no independent reproduction.
papers.relevance: Direct temporal-interface prior work, predating modern text-backbone duplex releases.
papers.limitations: Clock alignment does not itself establish correction-sensitive reasoning; dedicated released checkpoint not located.

comparison: Llama 3-8B with deduplicated HuBERT units (25 Hz before deduplication); periodic speaker/chunk tokens align the sequence to a real-world clock. Speculative user chunks are replaced by observed input.
Synchronous full-duplex scheduling despite variable token counts; evaluates processing/network delay.
Official paper/demos; model code/weights not located. Clock alignment alone does not establish revision correctness.

papers.title: Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue
papers.problem: Open foundation for the supplied paper; it already uses a pretrained LLM backbone.
papers.method: Helium 7B text LM + Mimi codec Synchronized user-audio, assistant-audio and assistant-text streams at 12.5 Hz. Temporal transformer models time; depth transformer predicts residual codec levels. Text inner monologue precedes acoustic generation; learned silence and overlap patterns.
papers.results: Paper reports 160 ms theoretical and approximately 200 ms practical latency under its setup.
papers.relevance: Open foundation for the supplied paper; it already uses a pretrained LLM backbone.
papers.limitations: Frame timing limits text bandwidth; basic inner monologue is not a private reasoning implementation.

comparison: Mimi 12.5 Hz (80 ms) frames; temporal transformer plus depth transformer model parallel audio streams and aligned inner-monologue text.
A concrete shared acoustic grid, streaming speech generation, and low-latency duplex interaction.
Inference and fine-tuning code + weights. MIT/Apache code; model CC BY 4.0. A frame clock is not a semantic commitment policy.

papers.title: DuplexSLA: A Full-Duplex Spoken Language Model with Synchronized Speech, Language, and Action
papers.problem: Speaking, listening and structured actions need a shared temporal protocol.
papers.method: 160 ms shared clock; two listening features, one text/four audio outputs, bounded action tokens and queued action spillover.
papers.results: Authors evaluate integrated duplex/tool behavior on a reported 2,100-case benchmark; no independent reproduction.
papers.relevance: Very close prior work for explicit action/speech/listening synchronization.
papers.limitations: Official repository marks inference, checkpoints and benchmark as forthcoming at cutoff.

comparison: Step-Audio 2 mini-derived ~7B model. A 160 ms clock joins two 80 ms listening features, one text/four audio tokens, and up to ten action tokens; queued action spillover and dual-side ASR.
Native concurrent speaking/listening plus timestamp-aligned planning, control and tool events.
Official repository says inference, weights and benchmark are forthcoming. Not a released checkpoint as of cutoff.

papers.title: AdaptDuplex: from static to adaptive full-duplex spoken dialogue
papers.problem: Very recent alternative for controlling the timing/capacity trade-off.
papers.method: Adaptive windows and bounded text lead; indexed backend launch/cancel; cancelled/stale results suppressed before injection.
papers.results: Reports 72.9 Final score on HumDial-FDBench; interruption and rejection have separate trade-offs.
papers.relevance: Cancellation alone is already implemented; joint speaker-owned result/output commitment must be differentiated.
papers.limitations: Paper verified; trained checkpoint and training package not located at the review cutoff.

comparison: Qwen3-Omni Thinker/Talker; 0.48/0.64/0.96 s windows, bounded text lead, and up to four indexed backend jobs. Cancelled/stale results are suppressed before injection.
Adaptive granularity and explicit backend-result admission already exist; not a new idea to simply cancel a stale job.
Paper verified; dedicated code/checkpoint not located. Joint speaker-owned state and actual playback still need controlled tests.

papers.title: Synchronization and Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue Models
papers.problem: Determine whether speaker/listener hidden states synchronize and encode turn-taking signals.
papers.method: Moshi--Moshi appointment conversations; lagged CKA and causal end-of-interpausal-unit probes under noise/activity-bias variation.
papers.results: Authors report near-zero-lag coupling that degrades with noise and useful timing probes; no causal correctness guarantee.
papers.relevance: Representation-level synchronization evidence complementary to runtime clocks.
papers.limitations: Restricted conversational task; artifact package not located; probe quality is not revision correctness.

comparison: Moshi--Moshi appointment dialogues: lagged CKA compares speaker/listener hidden states; causal probes classify end-of-interpausal-unit hold/non-hold events.
Representational coupling and predictive timing signals vary with noise and speech activity bias.
Preprint; study artifacts not located. Restricted task; CKA/probe success is not causal reasoning consistency.

papers.title: τ-Voice: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents on Real-World Domains
papers.problem: 278 airline / retail / telecom tasks; clean and realistic accents/noise; simulated full-duplex user.
papers.method: 278 airline / retail / telecom tasks; clean and realistic accents/noise; simulated full-duplex user. Metrics: Grounded pass@1; latency, interruptions and voice interaction quality.
papers.results: Original study reports voice-task success below its text baseline under both audio conditions.
papers.relevance: End-to-end task completion and correction consequences.
papers.limitations: Pin the task revision and simulator/provider configuration. Paper-clean, realistic and macro-domain scores are different conditions.

comparison: 278 airline/retail/telecom tasks; clean/realistic speech; full-duplex simulated user. ICML 2026 (PMLR 306).
Grounded pass@1, interruption behavior and voice interaction quality; tool/task consequences.
Code/tasks/simulator; provider APIs needed. Virtual time decouples simulation from wall-clock runtime; pin original revision (repo now tau3-bench).

papers.title: Full-Duplex-Bench-v3: Benchmarking Tool Use for Full-Duplex Voice Agents Under Real-World Disfluency
papers.problem: Real human audio; five disfluency types; chained tool calls in four task domains.
papers.method: Real human audio; five disfluency types; chained tool calls in four task domains. Metrics: Tool selection F1, argument accuracy, pass@1, first response / tool / completion latency.
papers.results: Authors identify self-correction and hard multi-step reasoning as recurring failures.
papers.relevance: Self-corrections, hesitation and multi-step tool reasoning.
papers.limitations: Tool-selection F1 is not task completion. Judge-assisted and exact argument matching differ.

comparison: Human recordings, five disfluency types, chained tools across four task domains.
Tool-selection F1, argument accuracy, pass@1; first response, tool and completion latencies.
Scoring/inference code + recording download. Tool F1 is not task success; exact and judge-assisted argument scores differ.

papers.title: EchoChain: A Full-Duplex Benchmark for State-Update Reasoning Under Interruptions
papers.problem: A model can acknowledge an interruption while its subsequent task-state reasoning remains wrong.
papers.method: Speech-onset-relative controlled interruptions, paired half-duplex control, and conversation-specific human-audited rubrics.
papers.results: Authors report no evaluated model above 50% conversation pass rate across 200 interrupted conversations; result not reproduced here.
papers.relevance: Direct benchmark predecessor for correction-sensitive ongoing reasoning.
papers.limitations: Four closed models; no backchannel/side-speech coverage or detailed acoustic timing; separate runnable release not located.

comparison: 200 controlled interrupted conversations; synthesized user/barge-in audio; four closed realtime models; paired half-duplex control.
Conversation/criterion pass rates and failures: contextual inertia, interruption amnesia, objective displacement.
Paper, prompts and examples verified; standalone code/audio release not located. Does not cover backchannels, side speech or detailed acoustic timing.

papers.title: Duplex-MPE: Benchmarking Multi-Party Interaction in Full-Duplex Dialogue
papers.problem: 2,000 matched scenario pairs / 4,000 streams; 3–4 human roles plus an assistant; explicit versus implicit address.
papers.method: 2,000 matched scenario pairs / 4,000 streams; 3–4 human roles plus an assistant; explicit versus implicit address. Metrics: Fresh response initiation, answer accuracy, silence preservation and floor release.
papers.results: Shows that frequent speech can coexist with wrong answers and failures to remain silent.
papers.relevance: Closest recent benchmark for the proposal’s multi-party speaker/stream-aware goal.
papers.limitations: Scenario roles do not imply natural human recordings. Floor release depends on whether the model was speaking.

comparison: 2,000 matched pairs / 4,000 synthetic streams; 3--4 human roles plus assistant; explicit/implicit address.
Response initiation, answer accuracy, silence preservation, floor release; speaker-owned update controls.
Paper verified; standalone code/audio release not located. Floor release is conditional on the assistant already speaking.

papers.title: Mind-Paced Speaking: A Dual-Brain Approach to Real-Time Reasoning in Spoken Language Models
papers.problem: Full pre-response reasoning delays speech; interleaving may disrupt reasoning continuity.
papers.method: Concurrent formulation/articulation with shared Step-Audio 2 parameters; incremental thought segments and think-incomplete SFT.
papers.results: Authors report improved latency/quality trade-offs; their near-zero-latency configuration still depends on synthesis buffering.
papers.relevance: Established think-while-speaking predecessor, underlying Step-Audio R1.1 and referenced by StepAudio 3.
papers.limitations: Concurrent formulation does not establish correction-safe audible commitment; performance depends on the tested backbone/tasks.

papers.title: Context Spanning: A Communication Framework for Full-Duplex Speech Models and External LLM Backends
papers.problem: Fresh alternative to compressed backend conditioning; useful for evidence provenance.
papers.method: Moshi frontend + external text backend Backend text injected into duplex token frames through chunked causal prefill. Frontend independently produces speech after receiving raw reference text. Context injection must fit prefill + one decode step in an 80 ms frame budget.
papers.results: Reports QA and full-duplex evaluations with direct information injection.
papers.relevance: Fresh alternative to compressed backend conditioning; useful for evidence provenance.
papers.limitations: Very recent preprint. Some experiments use precomputed backend answers with fixed delay; that differs from live tool execution.

themes: Acoustic frames, autoregressive tokens, physical elapsed time and audible commitments are distinct.
Full-duplex interfaces already encode timing, but do not by themselves establish causal reasoning-state consistency.
Model inference releases are more common than reproducible complete training mixtures.

gaps.text: Jointly measure evidence age, correct useful audible response time, and unsafe commitment under late corrections.
Maintain speaker-owned hypothesis versions across concurrent capture, reasoning, synthesis and playback.
Establish causal end-to-end consistency across corrected frontend state, pending tools and output queues, beyond cancellation alone; distinguish VoiceChat's tool-execution listening restriction.
Validate adaptive temporal interfaces against real wall-clock deadlines and compute contention, not only virtual-clock task scores.
Construct auditable prefix-sufficiency, revision and addressee labels without future-evidence leakage or cross-corpus session contamination.

research_questions.title: Think while listening
research_questions.question: When is partial speech sufficient to begin useful reasoning, and when should an emerging hypothesis remain provisional?
research_questions.proposal_link: Semantic sufficiency and revision-aware partial-input supervision.
research_questions.hypothesis: A trigger conditioned on available evidence and correction risk improves the correct-answer/latency frontier over end-of-turn and fixed-prefix triggers.
research_questions.method: Predict prefix sufficiency from causal input and track hypothesis versions; allow private inference before authorizing a task-specific spoken claim.
research_questions.experiment: 200 matched late-constraint questions with two suffixes sharing an identical prefix; compare end-of-turn, fixed-prefix and calibrated triggers under the same evidence and decode budgets.
research_questions.metrics: Correct useful audible response latency, final accuracy, premature-claim rate, calibration and unnecessary revisions.
research_questions.distinction: Early or latent reasoning while listening already exists; the candidate contribution is risk-calibrated revision under delayed/jittered evidence, not the concurrency claim itself.

research_questions.title: Think while speaking
research_questions.question: How far can reasoning and synthesis run ahead of playback without committing to an answer that new evidence will invalidate?
research_questions.proposal_link: Time to the first useful response and robustness to self-correction.
research_questions.hypothesis: Evidence-tagged output queues and a bounded playback lead reduce stale audible claims at matched response-quality and compute budgets.
research_questions.method: Separate private formulation from articulation, annotate queued output with evidence/state dependencies, revalidate unplayed output and repair already audible claims.
research_questions.experiment: Deliver a correction before generation, during synthesis, while queued, or after playback; compare unrestricted lead, fixed-duration lead and evidence-aware admission.
research_questions.metrics: Stale audible duration, useful-response latency, output underruns, repetition and repair success.
research_questions.distinction: Dual-process reasoning and bounded lead already exist. Test an explicit causal playback commitment boundary, rather than merely producing a faster first sound.

research_questions.title: Listen while speaking
research_questions.question: Can new input update the right speaker/task hypothesis while the system speaks, without mistaking backchannels or side conversations for corrections?
research_questions.proposal_link: Speaker/stream-aware listening and evidence integration across turns.
research_questions.hypothesis: Per-speaker evidence watermarks and selective state invalidation improve correction accuracy without increasing needless interruption or side-speech responses.
research_questions.method: Prioritize fresh input ingestion under generation load; associate updates with speaker, addressee, task and hypothesis versions before invalidating dependent output.
research_questions.experiment: Use matched corrections, backchannels and other-directed utterances with oracle versus predicted speaker/addressee labels; compare global versus speaker-owned state under matched load.
research_questions.metrics: Correction accuracy, evidence staleness, false interruption, silence preservation and task completion.
research_questions.distinction: Turn-taking and addressee tests are not new. The candidate is their coupling to causal reasoning-state ownership; attribution noise must be separated from reasoning failure.

research_questions.title: Synchronize listening, reasoning and speaking
research_questions.question: Which temporal interface remains reliable when speaking rate, inference speed, network delay and backend latency vary independently?
research_questions.proposal_link: Streaming latent state, uncertainty, and response preparation under partial evidence.
research_questions.hypothesis: A scheduler observing evidence age and audio-buffer duration has fewer missed deadlines and stale claims than fixed-window scheduling at matched task accuracy.
research_questions.method: Expose input watermarks, deadlines and predicted audio lead to the controller; adapt ingestion/generation quantum without using future speech or privileging one arm's compute.
research_questions.experiment: Replay identical dialogues across speech-rate, jitter and compute-contention conditions; compare fixed 80 ms/1 s interfaces where implementable with a two- or three-level adaptive controller.
research_questions.metrics: p50/p95 event-to-ingestion and correct-useful-response delays, buffer underruns, deadline misses, quality and GPU-seconds.
research_questions.distinction: Fixed clocks, adaptive windows and action alignment already exist. The target is a causal consistency/robustness claim under heterogeneous clocks; virtual-time results alone are insufficient.

research_questions.title: Revise while delegating
research_questions.question: What should be canceled, reused or withheld when a speaker correction arrives between backend launch, result return and audible delivery?
research_questions.proposal_link: Revision-aware hypotheses and late-arriving constraints; extension to modern asynchronous systems.
research_questions.hypothesis: Speaker/task-versioned dependency checks at both result admission and playback reduce stale-answer failures beyond an existing cancellation-only baseline.
research_questions.method: Tag jobs/results and output segments with dependencies, reject invalidated results, and recompute only affected work; use read-only or simulated tools in the pilot.
research_questions.experiment: Inject corrections into a simulated 0.5/2/5 s backend at launch, inflight, return and pre-playback stages; compare blind injection, explicit cancel/stale suppression, and joint result/output validation.
research_questions.metrics: Task success, stale-result use, wasted backend work, repair latency and unnecessary cancellation.
research_questions.distinction: AdaptDuplex cancels jobs and suppresses stale results; DuplexOmni stops/resets background thinking. VoiceChat's tool-execution barge-in restriction is a separate baseline condition. Candidate novelty requires speaker-specific dependency plus audible-commitment consistency, not renaming cancellation.

limitations: Availability snapshots can change; not located is not evidence of nonexistence.

Novelty is a bounded inference from these sources, not an exhaustive guarantee.
